sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: speed numbers, signaling, turns on red, turn lanes, roundabout yielding, J-turns, U-turns, right-lane exceptions, passing steps and backing
Confusable pairs from the traffic law pages, followed by continuation facts on speed, turns, roundabouts, J-turns, U-turns, right-lane travel, passing and backing; each block ties to one manual page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A01
The three default limits under ideal conditions are 10 mph in alleys, 30 mph on urban or town roads and 55 mph everywhere else, and posted signs override all three. [A01]
Why it matters: group speed limits; confusable alley versus town versus other roads; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A01
On two-lane highways posted at 55 mph or higher you may go up to 10 mph over the limit, but only while lawfully passing another vehicle. [A01]
Why it matters: group speed limits; confusable passing allowance versus the posted maximum; difficulty high.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A01
Driving faster shortens the time you have to react, raises the odds of a crash and makes serious injury or death in a crash more likely. [A01]
Why it matters: group speed; prereq for the basic speed law.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A01
A driver who reaches an intersection at an unlawful speed gives up the right-of-way they would have had at a lawful speed. [A01]
Why it matters: group speed and right-of-way; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A02
Going 20 mph or more over the limit adds extra fines, while going over 100 mph costs your driving privileges for at least six months. [A02]
Why it matters: group speed penalties; confusable extra fines versus revocation; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A02
Higher speed narrows your field of vision as well as raising the risk of a crash. [A02]
Why it matters: group speed; links to the reduced speed rules.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A02
Hand and arm signals are a daylight option only; at night, or when your vehicle hides your arm, rely on the turn signals. [A02]
Why it matters: group signaling; confusable day versus night signals.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-R08 | anchor: A03
Improper turns cause many crashes, so move into the correct lane well before the point where you will turn. [A03]
Why it matters: group turns; prereq for the left and right turn steps.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R09 | anchor: A03
Never make a sudden turn from the wrong lane, watch for traffic or obstacles on the road you are entering, and always end the turn in the correct lane. [A03]
Why it matters: group turns; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R10 | anchor: A03
If the car ahead is signaling a left turn, slow down and get ready to stop. [A03]
Why it matters: group turns; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R11 | anchor: A03
A right turn on red is allowed at many intersections, but a left turn on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto another one-way street, and both need a complete stop first. [A03]
Why it matters: group turns on red; confusable right versus left on red; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R12 | anchor: A03
When you turn right on red, watch for oncoming drivers turning left in front of you, since their green arrow may come on before your light turns green. [A03]
Why it matters: group turns on red; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R13 | anchor: A03
Stay out of other drivers' blind spots, and pay special attention to them near commercial vehicles. [A03]
Why it matters: group blind spots; links to sharing the road with large vehicles.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R14 | anchor: A04
A left turn ends in the first lane to the right of the center line, while a right turn ends in the lane next to the curb, and both use hand-over-hand steering. [A04]
Why it matters: group turns; confusable left versus right turn finishing lane; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-R15 | anchor: A05
Whenever you turn on a red light, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and where a No Turn on Red sign is posted, wait for the green light. [A05]
Why it matters: group turns on red; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-R16 | anchor: A05
Roundabouts are built to move traffic better and to make intersections safer than ordinary four-way stops. [A05]
Why it matters: group roundabouts; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-R17 | anchor: A05
Entering cars yield to cars already in the roundabout, but when two large vehicles go through a multi-lane roundabout side by side, the driver on the right yields to the one on the left, slowing or stopping if needed. [A05]
Why it matters: group roundabouts; confusable entry yield versus large-vehicle yield; difficulty high.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-R18 | anchor: A06
During the right turn at a J-turn you may cross both lanes into the left-turn lane in a single motion when it is safe, which shortens your time in the through lanes. [A06]
Why it matters: group J-turns; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-R19 | anchor: A06
When a rural divided highway has enough room between its roadways, you may cross one half, wait in the middle to the right of center, and cross the second half when it is safe. [A06]
Why it matters: group divided highways; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-R20 | anchor: A06
Turning left onto a divided highway follows the same steps as crossing it, and you must leave enough room that you do not slow oncoming traffic while you speed up. [A06]
Why it matters: group divided highways; confusable crossing versus turning left.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-R21 | anchor: A07
A U-turn reverses your direction with a half-circle turn, is allowed only when it will not disrupt other traffic, and is forbidden wherever a No U-Turn sign is posted. [A07]
Why it matters: group U-turns; prereq for the U-turn bans.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R22 | anchor: A07
On a roadway with two or more lanes in your direction, you may swing into the farthest lane and briefly use the shoulder to finish a U-turn when needed. [A07]
Why it matters: group U-turns; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R23 | anchor: A07
With only one lane in your direction, a driver going slowly enough to create a hazard must stay as close as possible to the right curb or road edge. [A07]
Why it matters: group right-lane travel; confusable one-lane versus multi-lane rule.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R24 | anchor: A07
You may use a lane other than the right-hand lane when passing, preparing a left turn at an intersection or into a driveway, preparing a left-side exit from an expressway, freeway or interstate, driving an authorized emergency vehicle, or following a traffic control device, a peace officer or work zone directions. [A07]
Why it matters: group right-lane travel; difficulty high.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R25 | anchor: A08
On the passing page one hundred feet appears twice: you must be back in the right lane before you are within 100 feet of an oncoming vehicle, and you may not pass within 100 feet of an intersection, underpass, tunnel or railroad crossing. [A08]
Why it matters: group passing; confusable return distance versus no-passing zone distance; difficulty high.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-R26 | anchor: A08
A single solid yellow line on your side bans passing for you, while a double solid yellow line bans passing for drivers in both directions. [A08]
Why it matters: group passing; confusable single versus double yellow; difficulty medium.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-R27 | anchor: A08
Take extra care passing at night, in poor visibility or on slippery roads, and before passing make sure oncoming traffic is far enough away and that nobody behind you is starting to pass. [A08]
Why it matters: group passing; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-R28 | anchor: A08
Signal left before moving out to pass and signal right after passing, then return to the right lane once the whole vehicle you passed shows in your rearview mirror. [A08]
Why it matters: group passing; difficulty medium.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-R29 | anchor: A08
Do not pass when you are about to meet an oncoming vehicle, and when someone is passing you, stay in your lane and do not speed up. [A08]
Why it matters: group passing; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-R30 | anchor: A08
A pass on the right must stay on the main roadway: using a bike lane, the shoulder or the unpaved edge to get around a vehicle is not allowed. [A08]
Why it matters: group passing on the right; difficulty medium.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-R31 | anchor: A08
Leaving a driveway in reverse, back only into the closest lane and then pull forward, and never reverse into or across traffic lanes unless you are sure it is safe. [A08]
Why it matters: group backing; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0037]
